text:
This was the perfect snapshot of Manchester City’s autumn difficulties. They simply cannot keep the door shut and looked like being picked off by Napoli, who had scored through Rasmus Højlund and Noa Lang either side of Ayyoub Bouaddi’s equaliser. Then Rayan Cherki, insistent but frustrated for most of the evening, seized the mantle five minutes from time and earned a welcome but deeply flawed draw. It meant Kevin De Bruyne, whose return last season had been ill-starred, was denied a deserved victory on his old home turf.
The buildup was largely a homage to De Bruyne, who was serenaded at the end of the warm-up and cheered upon the announcement of his name. It had all been done 14 months previously too, although back then De Bruyne lasted only 26 minutes, when a red card to Giovanni Di Lorenzo brought his sacrifice and an eventual 2-0 defeat. There have been few like the Belgian and his latest return was a luscious reminder, in these heavily asterisked times, of garlands collected under the same grim cloud.
In truth neither City nor a creaky Napoli, who are eighth in Serie A and functional rather than flowing, are the alluring propositions of days past. Beyond the De Bruyne appreciation ritual and a vocal performance from the visitors’ upper-tier contingent, this latest procedural wedge of league phase content commenced to near silence. City’s emergence in a new all-orange kit, apparently earmarked for selected Champions League games and timed handily for the festive season, added a degree of visual warmth to the late November chill.
Maresca needs his own tenure, stuttering amid selection uncertainties and questions over the team’s balance as well as the looming elephant, to catch light. Within a minute of kick-off Elliot Anderson came close to providing the spark with a low 20-yarder that Vanja Milinkovic-Savic parried unconvincingly. Anderson, scorer of a superb volley in Saturday’s otherwise laboured draw with Fulham, had kept his place in a side showing five changes.
City threatened again when Nico O’Reilly headed over at the far post and, even though Josko Gvardiol needed sound timing to stop a marauding Matteo Politano down the right, it was clear enough Napoli’s menace would not exceed the sporadic. As the half-hour approached Højlund shot tamely at Gianluigi Donnarumma from an angle but the concern for a ponderous City was that, since those early exchanges, they had shown little suggestion of conjuring a breakthrough. A considered ball in from Anderson, missed by a karate-kicking Erling Haaland, offered thin gruel.
Anderson sought Haaland again with a delivery that was shovelled behind for a corner. Napoli had hardly oozed composure but City’s speed of thought and movement had been too slow. When De Bruyne, manning the midfield alongside Scott McTominay and Billy Gilmour, fumbled possession inside his own half the hosts lacked sufficient zip to take advantage.
Haaland made contact with a Cherki cross but his header looped into the arms of Milinkovic-Savic. City had, at least, shown they could locate him. Shortly before half-time Napoli, firmly in the game, offered a precious glimmer of excitement when Sam Beukema’s header from a corner was batted away smartly by Donnarumma.
Napoli brought the first palpitations of the second half, too, when Lang briefly seemed to get in behind before O’Reilly recovered to stall his run. At the other end McTominay blocked from Cherki, atoning after his wild slash at the same player had put Napoli under some pressure. City had lacked width and wit all night so it was no surprise to see Jérémy Doku readying himself five minutes after the restart.
Doku arrived soon enough, replacing the anonymous Allan, but was turning away in despair within 30 seconds. This time Højlund’s bearings were perfect after taking a Gilmour pass and taking the ball outside a flailing Marc Guéhi, the finish cut sharply across Donnarumma and fizzed low into his left corner. Napoli had, to their credit, visibly upped things in the preceding spell.
Would City now do the same? Next cab off the rank was Iliman Ndiaye, with Enzo Fernández making way after a featureless showing. The slightest uptick in tempo and intent brought dividends. Doku had just slipped Anderson in for a shot well saved by Milinkovic-Savic when, from the resulting short corner, he was allowed to tee up Bouaddi 14 yards out.
The finish was swept in confidently and, given City’s previous toils, all too simply.
At last City had momentum, although the crowd’s newly discovered enthusiasm was channelled back towards De Bruyne when he was replaced in the 75th minute. Perhaps that interlude helped reverse the swelling tide. Immediately Leonardo Spinazzola, given acres down the right, crossed beyond the far post for Lang to volley in thrillingly.
City were spluttering again but Cherki, surging into a shooting position inside the box, crashed a fine strike past Milinkovic-Savic to secure parity.
digest_he:
מנצ'סטר סיטי המשיכה להציג יכולת פושרת לאחר שסיימה בתיקו 2-2 ביתי מול נאפולי במסגרת ליגת האלופות. החבורה של אנצו מארקה נקלעה לפיגור משערים של רסמוס הוילונד ונואה לאנג, כאשר באמצע השערים כבש אתיופ בואדי את השוויון הזמני עבור המארחים.

המשחק עמד בסימן חזרתו המרגשת של קווין דה בריינה לאצטדיון שבו כיכב בעבר, אך התוכניות של סיטי השתבשו בשל הגנה רעועה. בסופו של דבר, היה זה ריין שרקי שמנע הפסד ביתי מביך כשכבש שער שוויון בדקות הסיום והציל נקודה עבור קבוצתו.
